steps.note: Agent (Grok Bot, acting for Miles) given only the product name 'Neon' and the goal: get a working Postgres database with no human, A$0, then store and query known rows. Discovery restricted to public pages fetched live in this run.

GET https://neon.com/llms.txt -> 200 (41,280 bytes). Line 5 says: if the user cannot create an account, follow 'Claimable Neon' at https://neon.com/auth.md to provision Postgres without signup; a human claims it later. Chose this path (no human, no account, A$0).

GET https://neon.com/auth.md -> 200 (5,150 bytes). Checked preconditions it lists: NEON_API_KEY not set, 'neon' CLI not on PATH, so no existing account. Doc offers CLI or REST; chose the REST path (3 calls: register anonymous identity -> exchange for token -> fetch credentials) to avoid installing global packages on a shared machine. Requesting only the 'postgres' capability because that's all the task needs.

POST https://claimable.neon.tech/v1/agent/identity (anonymous, postgres only) -> HTTP 201. Got project restless-art-50105333; postgres capability granted=true; project expires 2026-10-12 10:08 pm AEDT unless a human claims it. Identity secret stored in a private file, not shown.

POST /v1/oauth2/token -> HTTP 200 (Bearer token, valid 3600 s). GET /v1/projects/restless-art-50105333/credentials -> HTTP 200 with a Postgres connection string (host *.aws.neon.tech, database neondb). Access obtained with no account, no human, no card. Credentials kept in a private file; never printed.

Expected end state written to expected.json BEFORE doing the work: table humanless_demo_orders with 5 known rows tagged with run tag hl-d1df48a8, plus an expected summary query result (implementation: 2 rows, A$75,000; pilot: 3 rows, A$13,500).

Tried a standard Postgres connection (port 5432) to do the work: timed out after 30 s. Network check: port 5432 to the database host is blocked from this machine, port 443 (HTTPS) is open. Nothing was written. Agent looks for an HTTPS route in Neon's public docs.

GET https://neon.com/docs/connect/choose-connection.md -> 200. Docs say the Neon serverless driver (@neondatabase/serverless) connects over HTTP/WebSocket instead of TCP. Agent switches to that driver over HTTPS (port 443), installed locally in the demo folder from the public npm registry (free).

Over HTTPS (Neon serverless driver 1.2.0, Node 20): created table humanless_demo_orders, inserted the 5 known rows, ran the summary query. Agent's own claim: implementation 2 rows / A$75,000; pilot 3 rows / A$13,500. Server: PostgreSQL 17.11. (This is only the agent's claim; it is checked separately below.)

honest_notes: First attempt to reach the database over the standard Postgres port timed out because this machine's network blocks that port; the agent found Neon's HTTPS route in Neon's docs and used that instead.
The agent's own report (step do_work) is not treated as proof; only the separate checker's verdicts are.
The checker is a separate Python program that shares no code with the agent and fetches its own fresh login from Neon before reading the data.
The language model behind the agent already knows public facts about Neon; the trace shows which public pages it actually read in this run.
All passwords, tokens and connection strings are left out of this trace.
